hero.title: The exchange that shows its books
hero.sub: Proof-of-reserves published every quarter and audited by a third party. Deep order books, real custody, and fees you can read on one page.

features.title: Built for people who read the fee schedule
features.sub: Everything an active trader checks before funding an account, published rather than buried.

items.title: Proof of reserves
items.body: A Merkle-tree attestation every quarter, audited independently, with a tool that lets you verify your own balance is included.

items.title: Deep order books
items.body: Spot, margin and futures on one book, with maker rebates from the first tier rather than the fifth.

items.title: Cold storage by default
items.body: 95 percent of assets held offline in geographically distributed vaults with multi-party signing.

items.title: A real API
items.body: REST and WebSocket, documented rate limits, and a testnet that mirrors production behaviour exactly.

items.title: Fees on one page
items.body: Thirteen tiers, published in full, with no hidden spread markup and no payment for order flow.

items.title: Institutional custody
items.body: Segregated accounts, qualified custodian arrangements and same-day fiat settlement in six currencies.

showcases.title: Custody that satisfies an auditor
showcases.body: Segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts held under a qualified custodian arrangement, with attestation reports issued quarterly and available to your auditors directly rather than through us.

testimonial.quote: They publish the fee schedule, the reserve attestation and the incident history on pages you can find without an account. Three things, and almost nobody else does all three.
testimonial.name: Rina Chaudhary

pricing.title: Fees, in full
pricing.sub: Thirteen tiers by 30-day volume. No spread markup, no payment for order flow.

items.q: How does proof of reserves work?
items.a: Balances are hashed into a Merkle tree that a third-party auditor verifies against on-chain holdings each quarter. A tool on the site lets you confirm your own balance was included in that tree, using a record only you can see.
About 95 percent in offline cold storage across geographically separated vaults with multi-party signing. The remainder is in hot wallets sized to cover expected withdrawals.
No. Revenue comes from published trading fees and the spread on fiat conversion, which is also published. There is no third party paying for the right to fill your orders.
Every outage since 2019 is listed on the status history page with the duration, the cause and what changed afterwards, including the ones that were our fault.

cta.title: Open an account in about four minutes
cta.sub: Identity verification is usually complete within the hour, and the fee schedule is on one page.

footer.tagline: A regulated exchange that publishes what most exchanges bury.

palette.name: Purple Deep
palette.note: The deepest purple — pressed and hover states

palette.name: Green
palette.note: Success and positive states, at 16% for badges

notes: Purple is the single brand accent and it carries CTAs, links and focus. Green appears only for positive or success states, never as a second brand colour.
The neutral ramp is cool and blue-leaning, not warm grey. That coolness is what makes the purple read as brand rather than decoration.
Radii sit at 12px — clearly rounded but never a pill. A pill CTA reads as consumer; this system is trading-desk.
Shadows are whisper level (rgba(0,0,0,.03) 0 4px 24px). They suggest a card edge rather than lifting anything off the page.
Numbers are the content. Use tabular figures everywhere a price, fee or balance appears.
